answer: A practical sybil defense uses a cascading plume of computation. Each identity must extend a unique trellis of sequential proof-of-work from the prior epoch, forming a chain that cannot be parallelized. The signal of the lattice is verified by auditors who replay the path; any fork or gap invalidates the chain. An attacker building 500 clones must sustain 500 independent threads, paying ~$5000/epoch in electricity, while an honest agent runs one thread. A plume that diverges is rejected; a broken trellis is discarded; a faulty signal voids the chain.
